Sedjem 0.3.6 makes a course from more places: a Google Drive folder, a folder on your computer, or several files
picked together. Google Drive files can be transcribed from their links, a whole course can be exported in one
step, and a YouTube video can stream instead of being downloaded.

## Download

- Windows 10 and 11: `Sedjem-0.3.6-setup.exe` installs for your user, without admin rights. It isn't
  signed yet, so SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher: choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
  Installing over 0.3.5 keeps your transcriptions, keys and models.
- Linux (x64): unpack `Sedjem-0.3.6-linux-x64.tar.gz` and run `Sedjem/Sedjem`.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums of both.

0.3.5 can update itself: *Settings → Updates*, then *Update now*.

## Changes

### Files

- A folder on this computer becomes a course: *Choose folder* in the desktop app, or its full path in the path
  field in a browser. Its recordings are listed in name order ("Lecture 2" before "Lecture 10"), you pick the ones
  to add, and each is read where it is, with nothing copied. Subfolders and other files are skipped and counted.
  Adding the same folder again adds to its course (#146).
- Several files dropped or picked together become one course, which you can name. Before, only the first of them
  was kept, and the others were dropped without a message (#146).

### Links

- The *Link* field (it was *YouTube*) takes a Google Drive file shared with anyone who has the link (#137).
- A Google Drive folder shared in the same way becomes a course of its audio and video files, in name order, with
  its subfolders skipped and counted (#141).

### YouTube

- Under *The video*, *Stream it from YouTube* downloads only the sound, so a long course takes much less space and
  time, and the page plays the video from YouTube. *Download the video* stays the first choice, and the form
  remembers the last one picked (#135).

### Exports

- *Export…* at the foot of the sidebar exports many transcripts at once: tick transcriptions, a whole course or
  all of them, pick one format, and get a zip with a file for each (a course's lectures numbered in a folder of
  their own) or one combined file in text, Markdown or JSON. In Chrome, Edge and the desktop app, the files can
  also go straight into a folder you pick. *Export course* on a lecture's page opens it with the course ticked
  (#134).

### Models

- *Settings → Models* has the *Default model*, the one a new transcription starts with, kept across restarts
  (#133).

### Assistants

- Under *What assistants can do* in *Settings → Assistants*, new switches let an assistant start transcriptions
  of YouTube and Google Drive links, and of recordings in folders you list, and choose a hosted model, which
  uploads the recording. Each is off until you turn it on (#140).
- A folder course, or a course of files, is listed with the other courses, with its title and never a path
  (#146).

### Under the hood

- sherpa-onnx 2.0.2, which labels speakers exactly as 2.0.1 did on six real meetings (#143), numpy 2.5.5 and the
  tools behind the tests (#144).

## Known limits

- Google Drive: Sedjem can't sign in yet, so a file or folder must be shared with anyone who has the link.
- The 3D-Speaker CAM++ speaker model can't be downloaded: its file changed on 19 November and Sedjem still
  checks it against the old one. A copy downloaded before then still works, and TitaNet-small and TitaNet-large
  download as before (#149).
- Browsers installed as Snaps, such as Ubuntu's Firefox, can't open files in hidden folders of your home folder,
  such as the Linux build's data folder `~/.local/share/sedjem`. There the desktop window opens Sedjem, or a
  browser that isn't a Snap.
